title: C17 · Three days of green tests and a dead button
anchor: Shipping tracking email crash, session 8 September 2026; and the 401 that was read as proof of deployment

slides.headline: THREE DAYS OF GREEN TESTS AND A DEAD BUTTON
slides.sub: Every test in the platform passed. The one button a rep needed most did nothing.
slides.boundary: No client data appears in this document.

slides.h2: WHAT I BELIEVED ON DAY THREE
slides.boundary: The suite was not lying. It had never been asked the question.

slides.h2: A TEST PROVES THE THING IT TOUCHES
lede: The tests covered the functions underneath. The failure was in the wiring between the page and those functions, which no test had an opinion about.
So every check I ran agreed with me, and all of them were answering a different question than the one I thought I was asking.
slides.boundary: The button rendered. It simply had nothing behind it.

slides.h2: FOUR CHECKS THAT AGREE WITH YOU FOR FREE

items.text: A test suite that never loads the page a person uses
A deploy that reports success for shipping the old build
A login wall answering before your code does
A log with no errors in it because nothing ran

slides.boundary: A refusal from the front door is not evidence that the room behind it exists.

slides.quote: The build proves it, not the test suite. Open the page a human opens, and press the thing a human presses.
slides.src: Every claim of live now needs one screenshot of the working surface, taken after the deploy.
slides.boundary: I said a feature was live once when it was not. That is where this rule came from.

slides.h2: HOW I CLOSE A BUILD NOW

left.p: Tests pass, deploy reports success, mark it done, tell somebody it shipped.

right.p: Load the real page, press the real control, watch the real record change. Then mark it done.

slides.boundary: It costs about ninety seconds and it has caught four of these.

lede: Your process document says the confirmation goes out. Your inbox says the mail merge ran. Neither of those is a client holding a confirmation.
Pick the one thing you are most sure works because a report says so. Then go be the customer for five minutes.
slides.boundary: The report is a claim. The click is the proof.

slides.h2: BUILT BY SOMEBODY WHO USES IT
lede: I sell promotional products for a living, so every one of these gets found the hard way, on a working day.
